newsitem.title: INDIA: India delegates more powers on mining to states.
newsitem.headline: India delegates more powers on mining to states.

text.p: India said on Friday it delegated powers for renewal of prospecting licences and mining leases to state governments, which until now required the approval of the federal government.

"The central (federal) government today announced the delegation of powers for renewal of prospecting licences and mining leases to state governments," Steel and Mines Minister Birendra Prasad Baishya told reporters in the Indian capital.
Baishya also announced the setting up of a government committee to suggest measures to delegate even more powers to states in the sector.

"The committee would also look into the question of steps for stopping illegal mining, streamlining of procedures pertaining to grant prospecting licences and mining leases...," a Mines Ministry statement said.

A government statement quoting Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said 36 foreign investment mining proposals worth over $500 million had been approved by the government under India's economic liberalisation programme launched in 1991.
"No foreign investment proposal is pending. All have been cleared," Baishya said.
In 1993, India opened up the mining of 13 minerals, previously reserved for the state sector, to private firms.
It also invited private investment and greater participation in the mining sector.

In October, India eased foreign participation rules in the mining sector saying foreign equity stakes of up to 50 percent in mining companies would be automatically approved, except in the case of gold, silver, diamonds and precious stones.

"I do feel that with the new dispensation, we would be able to attract large private investment and induct foreign capital and state-of-the-art technology in exploration and mining with the active participation of the state governments," Baishya said.
He said investments in the mining sector could help India achieve its target of attracting $10 billion in foreign investment in every year.
"Exploration and mining is an area which can well attract a foreign investment of $2 billion (annually)," Baishya said.
